chassis.note: 17.25 W x 9.5 D x 1.75 H in (43.82 x 24.13 x 4.45 cm), one figure for the line on every edition of the data sheet (the data sheet's own order is W x D x H). Converted to 438.15 x 241.3 x 44.45 mm. 438.15 is the body without brackets: the rack mounting guide fits them as separate parts (1U page, step 1). The data sheets give 6.4 to 7.2 lb for the line and no weight per model, so none is stated.

colour.note: medians of the photographs: the front face #313131 with an orange trim line along its bottom edge #f2ab49, the rear face plate #d4d4d4 inside a black lip #202020.

ears.note: Rack Mounting Guide 590-1510-501C, page 1, the 1U figure: the two brackets are fixed to the sides at the inlet face, standing at the front plane, so the shipped position is flush. The guide numbers no part for the brackets and no figure dimensions them. Page 2 shows a 0U mount with brackets in one of three slots; it is not modelled (gaps). The ears are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the single-AC front photograph. The inlet module sits at the left with the power switch above the inlet; the inlet is a C14 turned a quarter turn, as the photograph shows its three contacts. The printed Vertiv mark and wordmark start 67.5 mm in; the product name Avocent ACS8000 ends 6.2 mm from the right edge. DIGITAL IN and SENSOR are RJ45 jacks in white bezels, 24.3 mm apart. The six USB ports are three stacked pairs in silver frames 19.7 mm apart, under a bracket that carries the USB symbol. The SD card slot is a strip 25.2 mm long under the printed SD CARD. The small symbols printed beside the two caution triangles are too small to read in an 800 x 600 photograph and are not drawn.

lamps.note: Installer/User Guide Table 1.2: the STATUS lamp is green when the unit is fully booted, P1 green when power supply 1 is on, P2 green when power supply 2 is on. Table 1.5 gives each serial jack a green and a yellow lamp, with the meanings written under each lamp. This unit has one supply and the photographs of the rear carry both P1 and P2: the rear photographs do not name their model and P2 is drawn as printed.

method.note: NO DRAWING IS HELD, SO EVERY POSITION ON BOTH FACES IS MEASURED OFF THE MAKER'S PHOTOGRAPHS AND IS ESTIMATED. The rear is the 16-port photograph (3600 x 2327 pixels), taken near straight on: the face is 3280 pixels across for the 438.15 mm body, 7.486 pixels per millimetre. That scale is a feature of stated size and is checked by a second quantity: the serial jack pitch reads 105.3 pixels in that photograph and 25.0 pixels at 1.767 pixels per millimetre in the 48-port photograph, 14.07 and 14.15 mm. A rear position is good to about 0.5 mm across and 1 mm down. The front is the single-AC photograph (800 x 600 pixels, 1.767 pixels per millimetre across the same width): its positions are good to about 1 mm. Down the face both photographs look slightly down on the unit, so every y is taken from the bottom edge of the face with the same scale, which leaves a black lip 4.5 mm deep along the top of both faces. Counts and colours are read directly. The 32-port and 48-port rear photographs are 800 x 600 and are used for the run lengths and the gutters only; every y and the left cluster are the 16-port photograph's.

port-numbering.note: Printed numbers 1 to 8 on tabs under the jacks, a pair under each column: the odd number on a white tab at the left and the even number on a black tab at the right. Which jack of a column takes which number is not shown by any held document; the upper jack is taken as the odd port and the lower as the even. That assignment is an estimate. Ports 1 and 2 sit under the printed MULTI PROTOCOL bracket, the first column, and the Quick Installation Guide says the first two ports are multi-protocol.

power.note: Data sheet power usage: nominal 120 VAC typical 0.13 A and 6.2 W, maximum 0.47 A and 28 W; nominal 240 VAC typical 0.10 A and 7 W, maximum 0.29 A and 28 W. 28 W is the maximum at both voltages and is filed as `power-max-w`; the two typical figures differ by voltage and are in `power-usage`. The inlet is printed 1X - 100 - 240V, 1A, 50/60 Hz.

rear-layout.note: From the 16-port rear photograph. At the left: LAN 1 over LAN 2 as two RJ45 jacks in one white plate, each with a green lamp at the left and a yellow lamp at the right; then two SFP cages one above the other in a grey frame; then the console jack over two stacked USB ports in a white plate. The serial jacks follow in two rows, a ganged shell per run of columns: 4 columns in the 8-port model, then 4, 4, 8 and 8 as ports are added, 14.07 mm between columns and 6.24 mm between runs. Each jack carries a green lamp and a yellow lamp. The three lamps STATUS, P1 and P2 are at the right edge.

serial-ports.note: Data sheet hardware specifications: up to 48 RS-232 serial ports on RJ45, the first two selectable between RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485, one RS-232 console port on RJ45. The data sheets give an automatic Cyclades and Cisco pin-out conversion as a benefit.

serial-role.note: The serial ports are console server ports. Installer/User Guide, p.47, CAS Profile: "provides remote access to serial RS-232 console ports on your devices"; p.45: "Serial ports are set to the CAS Profile and disabled in the factory configuration". The same guide, p.39, lets a port take other profiles (dial-in, dial-out, power, socket client). The RJ45 console port is the local console (guide, p.9, Table 1.1: "Console port for connecting a terminal or workstation").

sku.note: The data sheet ordering table lists the part as "8-port unit single AC power supply". The other ACS8000 part numbers (dual AC, DC, modem, cellular) are not modelled by this device, and the rear photographs do not name their model.

The EMEA edition of the data sheet (the -404 part numbers) and the APAC edition AV-12339-APAC (07/24) carry the same specifications and the same dimensions. Avocent ACS8000 Advanced Console System Quick Installation Guide 590-1483-501E, page 1 figure: the numbered callouts and the note that some models have no SD, modem, USB or sensor ports on the front. Avocent ACS8000 Advanced Console System Rack Mounting Guide 590-1510-501C, page 1 and 2 figures: the 1U and 0U brackets. Vertiv Avocent ACS800/8000 Installer/User Guide (PDF built 2025-03-05), Tables 1.1 to 1.5: the callouts, the multi-protocol ports, the status lamps and the serial lamp states. The maker's product photographs of the single-AC front and of the 8, 16, 32 and 48-port rear faces. No dimensioned drawing, 3D model or stencil is held.
